### Recent comparator supplement, 6 October 2026

The following published studies were assessed in later primary-source notes and already inform the [connected account](CONNECTED-GENERATIVE-MODEL.md#acquired-distinctions-change-enacted-participation). This supplement brings their evidence and limits into the ledger while preserving the earlier selected table. Packages 38–40 preserve sources and reading scope; their preservation checks are not experimental replications. No raw-data reanalysis, new experiment or scientific rerun accompanies this addition.

| Connection and actual unit | Evidence retained | Comparator and identified limit | What would change the interpretation |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Encounter → altered material organization → subsequent participation.** Kramar and Alim's (2021) Physarum networks. | The [structural-memory comparison](../../../_process/research/2026-10-05-generative-foundation-review/root-foundation/PARTICIPATION-CONSEQUENCE-COMPARATORS.md) records stimulus-related tube-diameter changes and their persistence, with geometry-dependent responses. [Package 38](../../../sources/38-participation-consequence-2026-10-06/README.md) also preserves Reiber and Nogueira Júnior's published criticism. | Remodeling is observed; controlled acquisition, retention and later retrieval from assigned prior histories are not established by that observation alone. The letter contests the stronger memory interpretation without showing that the diameter changes disappear. Immediate stimulation and flow-based explanations remain relevant. Tubes within one network are not independent organisms. | Assigned prior encounters followed by a common later challenge, and a targeted change of the proposed retained structure, could test history-dependent use while controlling direct residual stimulation and general impairment. These are proposed discriminators, not performed tests in this synthesis. |
| **Earlier activity → changed subsequent plasticity.** Hulme and colleagues' (2012) acute rat hippocampal slices. | The [physiological comparison](../../../_process/research/2026-10-05-generative-foundation-review/root-foundation/CONSEQUENCE-ORGANIZATION-COMPARATORS.md) records priming-dependent changes in a later conditioning response and interventions constraining induction mechanisms. [Package 39](../../../sources/39-consequence-organization-2026-10-06/README.md) preserves the primary article and inspected figures. | A history-dependent change in plasticity is more specific than a fitted behavioral learning rate. Induction interventions do not locate the mechanism that retains and later expresses that change. The study does not establish beneficial learning, acquired stopping criteria or concern; the relevant expression mechanism remains unresolved. | An intervention after induction but before a matched later challenge, with appropriate controls and rescue, could distinguish a retained contributor from altered input delivery or general loss of responsiveness. A benefit claim additionally needs independently assessed consequences for continued functioning. |
| **Available information → choice of further inquiry or action.** Beran and Smith's (2011) experienced macaques and capuchins. | The [information-seeking comparison](../../../_process/research/2026-10-05-generative-foundation-review/root-foundation/INQUIRY-INTERFACE-COMPARATORS.md) records both bypassing unnecessary reveals and omitting needed information in the supplied matching task. Four of the original eight macaques met all final criteria; no capuchin did. [Package 40](../../../sources/40-inquiry-interface-2026-10-06/README.md) preserves the manuscript and inspected task figure. | The supplied menu and visible informational conditions do not isolate an internally acquired uncertainty criterion. Prior training and an ordinary stateful associative policy remain alternatives to a unique metacognitive explanation. Selection of successful animals for the early-trial analysis limits generalization. | Vary usable information retained from an earlier action while matching the later display and available operations; include changed applicability and unsuccessful cases. A stronger interface-revision claim must identify a retained change in effective access, rather than only an apparatus change. |

Package 38 also preserves Sonoda and colleagues' (2012) hermit-crab extension experiment. Its rapid adjustment to changed shell geometry constrains a simple collision explanation, but the separate-group comparison does not identify a retained within-animal learning history or subjective ownership. It is a boundary comparator in the linked note, not a further stage of the Physarum experiment.

Together these comparisons sharpen three different identification questions: whether a particular retained history is used, whether it changes later acquisition, and whether further inquiry depends on available information. They do not provide one observed developmental lineage or establish that inquiry's consequences generate a warranted criterion for stopping. The [current inquiry-sufficiency result](../../../_process/research/2026-10-05-generative-foundation-review/root-foundation/INQUIRY-SUFFICIENCY-INTEGRATION.md) is instead a reconstruction of saved computational histories and a conditional mathematical composition. Neither evidence type supplies the other's missing realization, and neither derives ethical authority from successful performance.
